record.original_question: For free-energy functions ψ(A,θ) of elastic crystals, characterize the displacement boundary portions ∂Ω1 and boundary data g for which the minimum of Iθ(y)=∫Ω ψ(Dy,θ) dx over deformations y with y|∂Ω1=g is attained, and characterize those for which it is not; in particular, determine whether non-attainment associated with microstructure is generic or exceptional.

evidence.quote: Problem 17. For free-energy functions ψ(A, θ) of elastic crystals, determine for which ∂Ω1 ⊂ ∂Ω and g : ∂Ω1 → R3 the minimum of Iθ (y) = ψ(Dy, θ) dx in A = {y ∈ W 1,1 (Ω; R3 ) : y|∂Ω1 = g} is attained, and for which it is not.
For example, is non-attainment generic or exceptional?

artifact.category_tag: calculus of variations in nonlinear elasticity
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ R^3 be a bounded Lipschitz domain representing the reference configuration of an elastic crystal, and let ψ : M^{3×3} × R → R ∪ {+∞} be a free-energy density depending on the deformation gradient A ∈ M^{3×3} and the temperature θ > 0, with ψ(·,θ) typically possessing multiple energy wells reflecting crystallographic symmetry (so that ψ(·,θ) is not quasiconvex in general). For a (relatively open) portion ∂Ω_1 ⊂ ∂Ω of the boundary and a map g : ∂Ω_1 → R^3, define the admissible set
   A = { y ∈ W^{1,1}(Ω; R^3) : y|_{∂Ω_1} = g }
and the energy functional
   I_θ(y) = ∫_Ω ψ(Dy(x), θ) dx.

(a) Characterize those pairs (∂Ω_1, g) for which the infimum of I_θ over A is attained by some y ∈ A.

(b) Characterize those pairs (∂Ω_1, g) for which the infimum is not attained (so that minimizing sequences develop finer and finer microstructure).

(c) In a suitable precise sense (e.g. with respect to natural topologies or measures on the data (∂Ω_1, g)), determine whether non-attainment associated with the formation of microstructure is generic or exceptional.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a well-known open problem in the variational theory of nonlinear elasticity concerning attainment of energy minima for non-quasiconvex multi-well energies. While partial results exist for specific boundary data lying inside or on the boundary of the quasiconvex hull of the energy wells (e.g., rigidity results of Ball–James, Dolzmann–Müller, Kirchheim, and others giving sufficient conditions for attainment or non-attainment), no general characterization of the data (∂Ω_1, g) is known, and the generic vs. exceptional question for non-attainment remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems in elasticity
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 17 asks to characterize boundary data for which the minimum of the crystal energy is attained, and asks whether non-attainment is generic or exceptional.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as an open problem.
